en: The Sūtra of the Land of Akṣobhya Buddha, Scroll One, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema of the Yuezhi during the Later Han Dynasty. Chapter One:
Generating the Resolve and Receiving Wisdom. Chapter One: Generating the Resolve and Receiving Wisdom.
Thus have I heard:

At one time the Buddha was staying on Vulture Peak Mountain near Rājagṛha, together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus, all of whom were arhats—whose cycle of birth and death had been severed, who were free from further fetters, who had utterly destroyed the prison of bondage, who had attained mastery of mind and perfect wisdom, who had subdued all devas and nāga kings, who had accomplished what was to be done, who had laid down the heavy burden of all that remains to be done, who had obtained all that is to be gained through the liberation of right wisdom, and who had attained mastery of mind and boundless deliverance—with the sole exception of Ānanda.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra rose, knelt with his hands joined in reverence, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
"Excellent, O God among Gods!

In the past, when various bodhisattvas seeking the unsurpassed, true, and correct path practiced their virtues and gave rise to the resolve for enlightenment, they immediately attained their respective titles."

These bodhisattvas, through their dignified demeanor, compassionately mind and bring peace and security to the devas and the people of the world; they act as a source of stability and provide great comfort. Toward the masses of beings, they compassionately mind and settle them through their dignified demeanor, and with their vast bodies, they manifest unobstructed compassion for the devas and humans within the world.

All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the present and the past act as illuminators—providing illumination from the manifestation of light up to the illumination of the Dharma—causing them to reach the light of the Buddha, which is beyond all names.

If there are those who seek the bodhisattva path, they should, like the vows, practices, and illuminating wisdom of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of old, as well as their *saṃnāha* (armor) and entry into the title of virtue, hear this and train in it accordingly, and practice it with devotion.
"One who trains in this manner shall immediately achieve the state of an avaivartika and the unsurpassed, perfect,
and true path. The Buddha said, "Excellent, worthy Śāriputra!"
Your question is most excellent.

You have asked concerning the vows and practices of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past, their illumination, and their saṃnāhas that led them to their respective titles; you have brought to mind the bodhisattvas of the future so that they may receive and uphold them.
"Listen closely to this, Śāriputra!
Reflect upon it well; I shall explain for you the practices performed by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the past. Śāriputra said:
“Indeed, World-Honored One!
We wish and desire to hear it.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“There is a world named Abhirati; its Buddha is named Mahāmaudgalyāyana, who there preaches the Dharma for the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the practices of the six pāramitās.”
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra thought to himself:
"I wish to ask the Tathāgata, the God among Gods:
What is this world Abhirati, and what is the Great-Eyed Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, who teaches the Dharma to the Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and the practice of the six perfections?"
At that time, the Buddha, knowing the thoughts in the mind of the Venerable Śāriputra, addressed him, saying:

“To the east, a thousand buddha-fields from here, there is a world named Abhirati. Its Buddha is named Mahāmaudgalyāyana Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is preaching the Dharma for the sake of the bodhisattvas and those who practice the six pāramitās.”

At that time, a bhikṣu rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Tathāgata Mahāmaudgalyāyana, and addressed the Tathāgata Mahāmaudgalyāyana, saying:
"O, Heaven among Heavens!..."
"I wish to form vows like those of a bodhisattva and learn what ought to be learned. "In this way, Śāriputra,
the Tathāgata Mahāakṣa spoke to his bhikṣu, saying:"
"It is indeed extremely difficult for one who has made a vow to train in the path of all bodhisattvas. Why is this?
A bodhisattva must not harbor anger toward any human being, nor toward any form of life, whether flying or crawling."
"In this way, Śāriputra! That bhikṣu addressed the Tathāgata Mahāakṣi, saying:
'O God among Gods!'"

From this day forward, I resolve to attain the unsurpassed, right, and true path; with my mind, I shall encourage and assist it without ever abandoning it, for the sake of aspiring to the unsurpassed, right, and true path. I shall ensure that I am free from flattery and deceit, that my speech is ultimate sincerity, and that what I say is without discrepancy.

“O World-Honored One! If, having conceived this mind of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) and sincerely making such a vow for unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment, I should give rise to anger toward any among the people, the winged, or the crawling and wriggling creatures; or if my first thought should be to conceive the mind of a disciple or a *pratyekabuddha*; or if my second thought should be to conceive thoughts of lust; or if my third thought should be to conceive thoughts of sleep, or thoughts of various perceptions arising from praise; or if my fourth thought should be to conceive thoughts of doubt—until I have attained supreme, perfect enlightenment—I would be deceiving all those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, who are currently preaching the Dharma in immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, and infinite worlds.”
“O World-Honored One among Gods!

I have resolved upon this mind of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), and having truly made such a vow for unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment, if I should conceive a thought of killing, first; or if I should conceive a thought of stealing the property of others, second; or if I should conceive a thought of non-celibacy, third; or if I should conceive a thought of false speech, fourth; or if I should conceive a thought of regret, fifth—until I attain supreme, perfect enlightenment—I would be deceiving these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones: those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones among Gods, who are currently preaching the Dharma in incalculable, measureless, inconceivable, and infinite worlds.”
“O World-Honored One among Gods!

If, having conceived this mind of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) and sincerely making such a vow for unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment, I should conceive thoughts of reviling—first; or thoughts of harsh speech—second; or thoughts of folly—third; or thoughts of frivolous talk—fourth; or thoughts of wrong views—fifth—and continue thus until the attainment of supreme perfect enlightenment, then I would be deceiving all those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones among Gods, who are currently preaching the Dharma now in immeasurable, infinite, incalculable, and inconceivable worlds.”
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“When a bhikṣu acts in this way, he has donned the great saṃnāha-saṃnaddha (the armor of the great vow)—that is, when a bodhisattva-mahāsattva first gives rise to this resolve, his mind harbors no anger toward any people, nor does it harbor resentment toward any kind of living being, whether flying or crawling.”
“Śāriputra! At that time, because that bodhisattva mahāsattva is free from anger, he is named Akṣobhya; because he is free from anger, he dwells in the stage of Akṣobhya.”

The Tathāgata Mahāmaudgalyāyana, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, also rejoiced in this name; the Four Heavenly Kings also rejoiced in this name; Śakra, Lord of Devas, and Brahmā Sahāmpati also rejoiced in this name.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“That Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya addressed the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāmaudgalyāyana, saying: ‘O Devātideva!’”

"I have resolved upon this mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*), and having truly examined it thus, I shall not depart from my vow as one who seeks unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment. If I do not practice according to what has been spoken here, if I constantly fail to maintain the path of conduct obtained through discipline, or if I resolve upon the mind of omniscience yet desire to attain Buddhahood while failing to be a śramaṇa in every lifetime, failing to wear the patched robes in every lifetime, or failing to possess the three dharma-robes in every lifetime until the attainment of supreme perfect enlightenment, then I would be deceiving these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—the Buddhas, Gods among Gods, who currently reside and preach the Dharma throughout immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, and infinite worlds."

"O World-Honored One! If I have resolved upon *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), and if my vow to seek unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment is indeed so, yet if in every lifetime I do not constantly preach the Dharma for others, if in every lifetime I do not constantly act as a Dharma teacher, if in every lifetime the matters I speak of do not possess the unimpeded and lofty conduct, and if in every lifetime I do not possess immeasurable, lofty wisdom, and if in every lifetime, having become a śramaṇa, I do not constantly practice alms-gathering until the attainment of supreme perfect enlightenment, then I would be deceiving all these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, currently preaching the Dharma now in incalculable, boundless, inconceivable, and immeasurable worlds."

“O World-Honored One! Since I have resolved upon this mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*) and sincerely vow to attain unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment, may I not, in life after life, become a śramaṇa who does not constantly sit beneath trees, and may I not, in life after life, fail to constantly practice the three matters with diligence.”
What are these three? First, walking; second, sitting; third, standing.

If, throughout successive lifetimes, one gives rise to thoughts concerning the roots of sin—such as speaking falsely to deceive others, slandering or calumniating, preaching the Dharma to women for the sake of food, drink, or other worldly causes, or giving rise to attachment, laughter, or flirtatious gestures while preaching the Dharma—then until the attainment of supreme perfect enlightenment, I shall have deceived all those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones: the Buddhas, Gods among Gods, who are currently preaching the Dharma now in immeasurable, incalculable, inconceivable, and infinite worlds.
“O World-Honored One among Gods!

If I have conceived this mind of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge) and truly aspire thus for the sake of supreme, perfect, and true enlightenment, yet in every lifetime raise my hand to preach the Dharma, or in every lifetime see other bodhisattvas who do not conceive the Buddha-mind, or in every lifetime conceive the thought of making offerings to outside heterodox practitioners while abandoning the Tathāgatas, or in every lifetime sit upon a seat to listen to the Dharma [without practicing], until I achieve supreme perfect enlightenment—then I would be deceiving all these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones: those innumerable, infinite, inconceivable, and immeasurable Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones among Gods, who are currently preaching the Dharma in worlds throughout the ten directions.”

“O World-Honored One! Since I have resolved upon this mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*) and sincerely made the vow to attain unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment, if in life after life I should give rise to such thoughts as:
‘I shall give to this person, but I shall not give to that person.’”
Life after life, if one should form the thought:
"I shall establish meritorious gifts in such-and-such a place, and I shall not establish meritorious gifts in such-and-such a place";
life after life, if one should form such a thought:

"If I were to think, 'I always bestow the gift of Dharma upon this person, but do not bestow the gift of Dharma upon that person,' and because of such partiality toward those I have encountered throughout successive lifetimes—even to the extent of not sparing my own body or life—were I to fail to attain supreme perfect enlightenment, I would be deceiving all these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones: those innumerable, incalculable, inconceivable, and immeasurable Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, who currently reside and preach the Dharma in worlds throughout the ten directions."

“O World-Honored One! Since I have resolved upon this mind of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), and since my vow is truly for the sake of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment, may my mind remain without variation toward all bodhisattvas in every lifetime until I attain unsurpassed, perfect, and true supreme awakening.”
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“At that time, for such a bhikṣu, the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, acts as his guarantor.”
If the Tathāgata acts as a guarantor, then the devas, asuras, and the people of the world will also act as guarantors.
At that time, when the Great Eye Tathāgata acts as a guarantor, the devas, asuras, and the people of the world likewise act as guarantors.
The Buddha said:

"Furthermore, if there are bhikṣus or bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, with such a form and armor (saṃnāha), seek the unsurpassed, right, and true path, they shall all attain the unsurpassed, right, and true path of supreme perfect enlightenment."
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“That Bodhisattva Akṣobhya addressed the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāmaudgalyāyana:
‘O Heaven among Heavens!’”

I have resolved upon this mind of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-citta*), and having truly made such a vow for the sake of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment, I declare: when I attain supreme, perfect awakening, if there should be any among the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, or upāsikās in that land who possess evil deeds or who slander those with evil deeds, I would be deceiving all those Buddhas, World-Honored Ones—the Buddhas, Gods among Gods, who are currently preaching the Dharma in incalculable, immeasurable, inconceivable, and infinite worlds.
"Furthermore, O God among Gods!

I shall practice until I attain the unsurpassed, perfect, true path of supreme enlightenment, so that none of the disciples in my Buddha-field shall possess any evil or wrongdoing; I shall cultivate the Buddha-way until my Buddha-field is adorned and purified."
"O World-Honored One among Gods!

If I have given rise to this mind of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), and if I have truly made such a vow for unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment, yet I should emit semen even in my dreams, until I attain supreme, perfect awakening, I would be deceiving all those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones among Gods, who are currently preaching the Dharma in incalculable, infinite, inconceivable, and immeasurable worlds."
"Furthermore, O God among Gods!

From this time forth until I have accomplished the unsurpassed, perfect, true path of supreme enlightenment, may none of the bodhisattvas in my buddha-field who have left the household life to practice the Way lose their vital essence even in their dreams."
“O World-Honored One among Gods!

I have resolved upon this mind of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge), and if I have truly made such a vow for unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment, yet there are still impurities among the women of the world when I have attained supreme, perfect awakening—if there are women with such impurities within my Buddha-field, then I would be deceiving all those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones—those Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, who are currently preaching the Dharma in incalculable, measureless, inconceivable, and infinite worlds.”
“This is the practice of a bodhisattva’s Dharma-activity according to their mental resolve, and the Buddha likewise teaches the Dharma to them as is appropriate.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“At that time, there was a bhikṣu who spoke thus to the bodhisattva mahāsattva Akṣobhya regarding this formation of a vow:”
"If I am indeed one who shall not regress, I shall press the earth with my right finger and cause it to tremble greatly.
At that moment, the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya, responding to the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power and receiving its sublime and lofty strength, caused the earth to quake in six ways.
"Whatever is manifested by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya is exactly as he has spoken; there is no difference.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
"If there are bodhisattvas who wish to achieve the unsurpassed, true, and correct path of supreme perfect enlightenment, they should study the practice of the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya."

When a bodhisattva mahāsattva trains in the practice of the bodhisattva Akṣobhya, before long they shall likewise take hold of a buddha-field and shall further attain unexcelled, perfect, true, and complete enlightenment.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked the Buddha:
"O God among Gods!
When the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya first resolved his mind [upon enlightenment], how many devas were present in the assembly?"
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“When the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya first resolved his mind to train, all the Four Heavenly Kings, Śakra, the Māras, and Brahmās within the trichiliocosm turned toward the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya with palms joined and spoke these words:
‘We have never before heard of such a saṃnāha (armor/vow).’”
The devas, having heard this, spoke thus:
"When the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya attains unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment, if there is anyone born in that Buddha-field, that person’s merit will not be small."
The worthy Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:

“I have never heard of any other bodhisattva-mahāsattva training in saṃnāha with such a form and appearance as this. Neither have I seen nor heard of anyone, such as the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Akṣobhya, for whom the God among Gods has bestowed such a name.”
The Buddha said: "It is so, Śāriputra."
There are few bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who train in this armor and in unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment with such a form and appearance as the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Akṣobhya.
In this regard, Śāriputra!
“During the Bhadra Kalpa, the virtues of all those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do not equal the merit of the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Akṣobhya.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“At that time, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāmaudgalyāyana bestowed upon the bodhisattva Akṣobhya the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment.”

"You shall become a Buddha in the future, named Akṣobhya Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha; you shall perfect the practice of wisdom and serve as a teacher and father, a supreme great being who brings stability to the world, a charioteer of the Dharma, the Honored One above all gods and men—a Buddha, a god among gods."
"It was also like when the Buddha Dīpaṃkara bestowed upon me the prediction of my future enlightenment. Then the Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"When the Tathāgata Mahāmaudgalyāyana bestowed upon the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Akṣobhya the prediction of his unsurpassed, perfect, and true path to enlightenment, that trichiliocosm was filled with a great radiance."

It is just as when I, likewise, bestow the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment; at that time, this trichiliocosm becomes entirely filled with great radiance. Furthermore, Śāriputra!
When that Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya attained unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment and realized the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), this trichiliocosm shook in six ways;
likewise, when I too attained unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment and realized the wisdom of omniscience, this trichiliocosm shook in six ways.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya received the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment, all the medicinal herbs and trees within this trichiliocosm bent of their own accord toward the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya and paid him homage.

Just as I was likewise, when I attained unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment and realized the wisdom of omniscience (sarvajñatā), all the medicinal herbs and trees within this trichiliocosm bent of their own accord toward me and paid me homage."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāakṣobhya bestowed upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment, all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas within the trichiliocosm turned toward the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya with palms joined in salutation. It was just as it is with me:

when I attained unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment and realized the wisdom of omniscience (sarvajñājñāna), all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas of the trichiliocosm turned toward me with palms joined in salutation."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāakṣobhya bestowed upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment, all pregnant women throughout the trichiliocosm gave birth in safety; the blind regained their sight, and the deaf regained their hearing.

Just as it was then, so it shall be now: when I have attained unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment and realized the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), all pregnant women in this trichiliocosm shall give birth in safety; the blind shall regain their sight, and the deaf shall regain their hearing."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata, Arhat,

Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāakṣu bestowed upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment, all humans and non-humans throughout the trichiliocosm burned incense;
likewise, when I attained unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment and realized the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*), all humans and non-humans throughout the trichiliocosm burned incense."
The venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying,
“The bodhisattva mahāsattva Akṣobhya possesses such infinite virtues.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya possesses not only these merits; it is not merely the Tathāgata Mahācakṣus who has bestowed upon him the prophecy of his future enlightenment. He has attained such immeasurable, ineffable, and infinite merits as these.”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata Mahāakṣu bestowed upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment, the minds of all the devas, asuras, and people of the world were all set at ease, and they all attained their proper time. It is just as it was for me:

when I achieved unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment, the supreme awakening, and attained the wisdom of sarvajñatā, the minds of all the devas, asuras, and people of the world were all set at ease, and they all attained their proper time."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

When that Tathāgata Mahāakṣu conferred upon the Bodhisattva-mahāsattva Akṣobhya the prediction of unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment, the yakṣas and spirits constantly followed and protected him;
just as it was with me, when I attained unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment and realized the wisdom of sarvajñatā, the yakṣas and spirits constantly followed behind me."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata Mahāakṣu conferred upon the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Akṣobhya the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment— the most correct awakening— and [he] attained the wisdom of sarvajñatā (all-knowledge), the devas, asuras, and people of the world made offerings to him with celestial flowers and celestial incense;

just as it was for me, so too when I attained unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment— the most correct awakening— and attained the wisdom of sarvajñatā, the devas, asuras, and people of the world came to make offerings with celestial flowers and celestial incense."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata Mahāakṣu conferred the prediction of unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya, twenty billion people and thirty billion devas resolved their minds upon unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment; the Tathāgata Mahāakṣu, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, conferred the prediction upon them all."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāakṣu bestowed the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya, the earth shook greatly, and blue lotuses (utpala), red lotuses (padma), yellow lotuses (kumuda), and white lotuses (puṇḍarīka) spontaneously grew, covering the ground. It was just as it is with me:

when I attained unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment and realized the wisdom of omniscience (sarvajñatā), the great earth spontaneously produced blue lotuses, red lotuses, yellow lotuses, and white lotuses, which covered the ground."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata, Arhat,

Samyaksaṃbuddha Mahāmaudgalyāyana bestowed the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment upon the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Akṣobhya, hundreds of devas, thousands of devas, and hundreds of thousands of devas abided in the void and scattered celestial garments over the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya,
saying these words: 'This Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva shall transcend and attain unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment as the Most Righteous Buddha.'"

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata Mahāakṣu conferred upon the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Akṣobhya the prediction of unsurpassed, right, and true enlightenment, at that time the devas, asuras, and people of the world loved one another more intensely than parents love their own children. It shall be even so for me:

when I attain unsurpassed, right, and true enlightenment, the most perfect awakening, the devas, asuras, and people of the world shall love one another more intensely than parents love their own children."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra,

when the Tathāgata Mahāakṣu conferred upon the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Akṣobhya the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment, all the devas and humans within this trichiliocosm, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, heard that the prediction of enlightenment had been conferred upon the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya."

"In this way, Śāriputra! In the past, when the Bodhisattva was receiving his prediction [of enlightenment], the people of this land were single-minded in their practice of giving. For the sake of merit, they enjoyed fine food and drink; and if there were those who came seeking anything, they would give to them whatever they themselves delighted in."

It is just as with me: when I attained unsurpassed, perfect, true enlightenment as the Most Rightly Awakened One, all the devas and human beings within this trichiliocosm heard their own predictions of enlightenment through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power.
In this way, Śāriputra!

Formerly, the people of this land were single-minded in their practice of giving. For the sake of merit and for the pleasure of fine food and drink, whenever there was anyone who sought anything, they would give to them whatever they themselves delighted in.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Tathāgata Mahāakṣu conferred upon the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya the prediction of his unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment, all the devas of the desire realm sounded celestial musical instruments as an offering."
“Śāriputra! This is the meritorious conduct at the time when this Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya received his prediction.
The Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"It is difficult to fathom, O God among Gods!
The Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha has truly spoken of this—the inconceivable realm of the Buddhas, the inconceivable realm of the devas, and the inconceivable realm of the nāgas."
This inconceivable realm of the nāgas was obtained by the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya from the time he first resolved his mind upon awakening and began his training.
“O God among Gods!
This moment when the bodhisattva mahāsattva Akṣobhya receives his prediction is likewise inconceivable.
At that time, the venerable Ānanda said to the venerable Śāriputra:
“Is it thus that the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya first resolved his mind upon the training in the *saṃnāha* (armor) and attained such a title?
Śāriputra said to Ānanda: “All of these are brought about by causes and conditions;
the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Akṣobhya’s initial resolution of mind, his training in the *saṃnāha*, and his virtuous title—the Buddha shall now explain them in detail.”
Then the Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“The Bodhisattva Akṣobhya could cause space itself to change when he first gave rise to this resolve, but the vows I have undertaken cannot be made to change; such is the nature of his armor-clad perseverance (saṃnāha-saṃnaddha).”
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“Just as the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Akṣobhya has donned the saṃnāha-saṃnaddha (the armor of resolve), the bodhisattva-mahāsattva Ratnaśrī has likewise learned and practiced from the bodhisattva Akṣobhya.”

Śāriputra! Innumerable bodhisattvas cannot fathom the extremely firm saṃnāha-saṃnaddha (armor of resolve) donned by the bodhisattva Akṣobhya, nor the manner in which he has thus accumulated his store of virtuous conduct.
“Śāriputra! That Bodhisattva Akṣobhya has attained the unsurpassed, right, and true path and realized supreme perfect enlightenment; he currently resides in the world Abhirati.”

"When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, was practicing the bodhisattva path, from life to life, even when people sought his hands, feet, head, eyes, or flesh, he never went against their wishes."

“Śāriputra! From the time Akṣobhya Tathāgata first resolved his mind [on awakening] until he attained unsurpassed, perfect, true, and complete enlightenment, he never experienced a headache, nor did he suffer from wind-disorders or the ailment of suppressed phlegm.”
Śāriputra! These are the most difficult-to-attain and unprecedented dharmas of that Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path.

"When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he beheld the Tathāgatas in every lifetime and always maintained the pure conduct (brahmacarya) throughout all his lives; he did so in every birth. This is called the Bodhisattva Akṣobhya traveling from one buddha-field to another, and wherever he arrives, he constantly sees with his own eyes the sons of gods born among the gods."
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

It is like a wheel-turning monarch who has gained mastery over the world; from one palace to another, his feet never once tread upon the ground, and wherever he goes, he constantly delights himself with the five kinds of pleasure, enjoying sovereign freedom until the end of his life.”
Thus it is, Śāriputra!

When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya practiced the bodhisattva path, in every lifetime he always personally beheld the Tathāgatas, the Arhats, the Samyaksaṃbuddhas, and constantly cultivated the pure conduct (brahmacarya). Whenever those Buddhas preached the Dharma, he practiced all the pāramitās, while few followed the path of the śrāvakas.

The practice of his perfections (*pāramitā*) consists in preaching the Dharma—encouraging those established on the path of the Buddha to assist him by manifesting the truth, causing them to rejoice and leap with joy, and leading them all to cultivate the unsurpassed, right, and true path—and thus he gives rise to this most noble resolve:
"When he preaches the Dharma, may all the roots of virtue (*kuśalamūla*) held through his vows be dedicated toward the unsurpassed, right, and true path."

By means of these roots of merit, I vow that when I attain unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment and preach the Dharma, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas within my buddha-field shall, through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, receive, recite, and uphold it whenever the Buddha preaches the Dharma.

Having recited this, these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas travel from one buddha-field to another, their minds always delighting in the Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, until they attain unexcelled, perfect, true, and complete enlightenment.

"I am also like this: from one buddha-field I travel to another buddha-field, and there I abide in the Tuṣita Heaven, attaining the state of being 'one birth away from Buddhahood' (ekajātipratibaddha).
The Buddha spoke again to Śāriputra:
"In this way, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas descend from the Tuṣita Heaven by their own supernatural power into the womb of their mother and are born from her right side."
When the Bodhisattva was born and fell to the ground, the earth shook greatly; such is the natural response resulting from his cultivation.
While the Bodhisattva was in his mother’s womb, there was no foul odor, no impurities, and nothing disagreeable.
Then the Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"Suppose, for example, a bhikṣu with supernormal powers enters a gabled hall; he travels and wanders all around in mid-air, moving through the air within the gabled hall without encountering any obstruction or hindrance."
In this way, Śāriputra,
when a bodhisattva enters his mother’s womb, he is as if traveling and surveying all around in open space, without any contact or obstruction, and without any foul odors.
When that Tathāgata Akṣobhya formerly practiced the bodhisattva path, it was thus;

I too am likewise, and while practicing the unsurpassed, right, and true path, I have destroyed all demonic activities, and I have thus attained unsurpassed, right, and true enlightenment as the most perfect Buddha.

"In the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya, those who seek the bodhisattva path and the path of the śrāvaka all destroy all evils and subdue the multitudes of Māras until they are entirely exhausted; the people of that Buddha-field no longer engage in demonic activities, [thinking]:
'I shall cultivate this Buddha-way until I attain renunciation and study the Way.'"
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya—the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path and listening to the preaching of the Dharma, his body did not experience fatigue, nor did his mind think of fatigue.”
Śāriputra! When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya was formerly seeking the bodhisattva path, while listening to the preaching of the Dharma, he made this vow:
"May such excellent dharmas as these cause all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas within my buddha-field to likewise cherish such excellent dharmas."
2. Chapter on the Excellence of Akṣobhya Buddha’s Buddha-field. Chapter Two: On the Excellence of Akṣobhya Buddha’s Buddha-field. The Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“O God among Gods!
When this Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, was formerly practicing the conduct of virtue and establishing his name, he attained the title "Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
It is most excellent, O Devātideva!
May the Buddha further explain in detail the excellence and happiness of that buddha-field.

Why is this? Because those who seek the bodhisattva path, upon hearing and knowing the excellence and happiness of that buddha-field as well as the instructions manifested and practiced by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, [will be inspired].

Furthermore, if there are those seeking the path of disciples who have not yet attained liberation, they shall hear of the excellence and joy of that buddha-field, as well as the teachings manifested by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya and his reverent, pure conduct.
The Buddha said, "Excellent, excellent, Śāriputra!"
Your question is excellent; it is truly wonderful that you have thus reflected upon the excellence of the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya.

When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya attained unsurpassed, perfect, true enlightenment and realized the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), this trichiliocosm was filled with great radiance, and the earth shook in six ways.

"When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya attained supreme perfect enlightenment, all the people within that trichiliocosm did not eat or drink for seven days; yet they neither consumed food or drink improperly nor engaged in false flattery, and their bodies felt no sense of exhaustion."
It is so; they all conceive thoughts of peace and well-being, delighting in one another with love and respect, their minds filled with joy as they attain timely mindfulness.
At that time, all the people and the gods of the desire realm abandon defiled and turbid thoughts.

Why is this? It is because of the power of the vows made by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya in the past that he has attained this virtuous title; consequently, all the people throughout the entire trichiliocosm join their palms and direct them toward the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
Such is that buddha-field; no incalculable number of other buddha-fields can equal the excellence and joy of this Akṣobhya Buddha-field.
"Śāriputra, it is because of the vows held by this Tathāgata Akṣobhya when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path that this is so."
“Śāriputra, when the vows held by the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are fulfilled, the buddha-fields become excellent and sublime.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra, “In the past,
when I was practicing the bodhisattva path, I now naturally obtain everything just as I vowed.”

When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya attained unexcelled, perfect, true, and complete enlightenment, all the people of that trichiliocosm—both those who possessed the divine eye and those who did not—beheld his radiance.
“Śāriputra! This is because the Tathāgata Akṣobhya maintained the vows he made when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path.
The Buddha spoke again to Śāriputra:

"When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya attained unexcelled, perfect, true, and complete enlightenment and proceeded to the Bodhi tree, even the various malevolent Māras were unable to conceive such a thought; how much less could they have gone to disturb his omniscient wisdom?"
Śāriputra! This is because the Tathāgata Akṣobhya maintained the vows he made when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path. Furthermore, Śāriputra!

When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya attained unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment and realized the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*), incalculable hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of devas and humans abided in the void, making offerings with celestial flowers, celestial sandalwood, various fragrances, celestial powdered incense, and celestial music, scattering them over the Buddha Akṣobhya.

Having made these offerings, the celestial flowers, celestial incense, celestial powdered incense, celestial sandalwood incense, and celestial blended incense all remained suspended together in the void, transforming into a circular flower canopy.
Śāriputra! This is the power of the vows that the Tathāgata Akṣobhya made when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path.

The radiance of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya illuminates the entire trichiliocosm with constant light; the radiance of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya completely eclipses the radiance of the sun and moon, as well as the radiance of all the devas, causing them all to cease, so that the people no longer perceive the light of the sun and moon.
“Śāriputra! This is due to the upholding of the vows made by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path.
The venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“O God among Gods!

When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, by virtue of having donned this great saṃnāhasaṃnaddha (armor of resolve), did he then make such a vow?”
The Buddha said:

"In the past, when practicing the bodhisattva path, hundreds of thousands of people, and even incalculable, countless beings, accumulated roots of virtue. By means of these accumulated roots of virtue, they maintained their aspiration for unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment, vowing to attain the Buddha-way and purify their buddha-fields. Just as they desired to adorn their buddha-fields according to their vows, so too did they fulfill those aspirations."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, the tree of the Buddha Akṣobhya is made of the seven treasures; it is forty *li* high and twenty *li* in circumference. Its branches and leaves extend forty *li* sideways, and its branches hang downward. A railing encircles the tree, five hundred and sixty *li* in circumference. It was beneath this tree that the Tathāgata Akṣobhya attained the wisdom of omniscience (*sarvajñajñāna*)."
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"Suppose a skilled person in this world were to play a hundred kinds of musical instruments; their sounds would not equal the sounds of the stairways and trees in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya—when the wind rises and blows upon the stairways, the trees strike one another and produce a mournful sound."
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“Listen to the purity and bliss within the realm of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha; listen attentively and reflect upon it well, for I shall now explain it to you.”
The venerable Śāriputra said:
“Indeed, World-Honored One!
We wish and desire to hear it.”
The Buddha said:
“In the realm of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, there are no three evil paths.
What are these three? They are:”
First are the hells, second are the animals, and third are the hungry ghosts.
All people practice virtuous deeds.
"The ground there is level and even; the trees that grow there have no variation in height; there are no mountains, hills, ravines, or valleys, nor are there any pebbles or crumbling crags."
As for that ground, when one walks upon it with the feet, it sinks; as soon as the foot is lifted, it returns to its original state.
It is like a soft cotton pillow: when one rests their head upon it, it yields; as soon as the head is lifted, it returns to its original state; such is that ground.
"In that buddha-field there are no three kinds of illness.
What are these three? First, wind; second, cold; and third, gas."

"In that buddha-field, none of the people have unwholesome complexions, nor are there any who are ugly; their lust, anger, and delusion are thin. Among the people of that buddha-field, there is no matter of imprisonment or confinement in prisons, and there are none at all of the various heterodox paths."

"In that land, the trees always bear flowers and fruit; the people all take five-colored garments from the trees and wear them together. These garments are exceedingly beautiful, and none of them show signs of fading."
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“The fragrance of the garments worn by the people is like the scent of celestial flowers; the fragrance and flavor of their food and drink are as exquisite as the scent of celestial trees, never ceasing.”
"The people there wear various garments of immeasurable variety; furthermore, whatever food those people in that buddha-field think of, it immediately appears before them naturally.
For example, Śāriputra!"

Just as the food of the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven appears spontaneously before them according to their thoughts, so too, whatever food the people of that land desire in their thoughts, it appears spontaneously before them; among those people, there is no one who feels greed for food or drink.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
In that buddha-field, the places where the people lie down and rise are pavilions made of the seven treasures with latticed windows, filling [the land] without any empty spaces."

Within that bathing pool is water of eight flavors, which the multitude of people shares in common; this water flows and pours from one to another, so that none of the people ever lose their practice of the wholesome Dharma.
“Śāriputra, it is just as, for example, the precious jade woman surpasses ordinary women and cannot be equaled by them; her virtue is like that of a celestial maiden.
In the same way, Śāriputra, [the Bodhisattva]...”

If one were to compare the virtues of the women in that buddha-field to those of the Jewel of the Woman (strī-ratna), the Jewel of the Woman would not equal the women of that buddha-field by a hundredfold, a thousandfold, ten-thousandfold, a hundred-millionfold, or even a trillionfold; they could not be compared.
“The people have couches made of the seven treasures, spread over with fine cushions; all these arise spontaneously through the power of merit. Śāriputra!

This is because the Tathāgata Akṣobhya—the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—upheld the vows he made when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path; it is through the power of such merit that the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya Buddha has become like this.”
The Buddha spoke again to Śāriputra, saying:
"The food of the people in that land is superior to the food of devas and humans; its color, fragrance, and flavor are likewise superior to what is consumed by devas and humans."
"In that land there is no king, but only the Dharma King— the Buddha, the God among Gods.
The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!..."
For example, Śāriputra, just as the people of the continent of Uttarakuru have no king to rule over them,
so too, Śāriputra, in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya, there is no king; there is only the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the God among Gods— the Dharma King.
“Śāriputra, it is like this: for example, when Śakra, the Lord of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, forms a thought while seated, the devas immediately come to receive his instructions.
Śāriputra, such is the excellence and joy of the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.”
“The people of that land do not engage in sexual desire. Why is this?
It is because of the power of this Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, the Lord of Men, the God among Gods, Akṣobhya.”
“Śāriputra! This is due to the power of the vows made by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path, which has caused this buddha-field to be so excellent and delightful.
At that time, a certain bhikṣu, having heard this description of the merits of that buddha-field, immediately conceived a lustful thought regarding it and came forward to address the Buddha, saying:
“O God among Gods!
I wish to be reborn in that Buddha-field.
The Buddha then addressed that bhikṣu, saying:
“Fool! You shall not be born in that buddha-field. Why is this?

"One does not attain birth in that Buddha-field by establishing lustful and distracted thoughts; rather, one attains birth in that Buddha-field through other virtuous practices and pure dharmic conduct.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"In the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, there is water of eight flavors which all the people there share in common. If the people should think, 'May a natural bathing pool appear, filled with water of eight flavors,' then for the sake of those people, a natural bathing pool immediately appears, filled with water of eight flavors."
If he intends for the water to flow, it flows; if he intends for it to cease and disappear, it ceases and disappears.
That buddha-field is neither excessively cold nor excessively hot; breezes arise gently, being exceedingly fragrant and refreshing.

For the sake of the devas, nāgas, and human beings, this wind arises according to their thoughts. If a single person thinks they wish for the wind to arise and blow upon them, the wind will blow only upon that person;

if one thinks they do not wish for the wind to arise, the wind will not arise. When the wind arises, it does not disturb the bodies of people; the wind arises in accordance with what each person thinks.
"Śāriputra! This is the excellence and joy of the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, just as it was previously vowed.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"In the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, if women desire pearls, beads, or necklaces, they simply take them from the trees and put them on; if they desire garments, they likewise take them from the trees and wear them."
Śāriputra! In that buddha-field, women do not possess the feminine characteristics found among the women in my own field, Śāriputra!
"What are the characteristics of the women in my land?
The women in my land have ugly and unsightly appearances, foul tongues, envy toward the Dharma, and minds attached to perverse matters.
Such are the various traits of the women in my land; the women in that Buddha-land do not possess these traits."
"Why is this? It is due to the power of the vows made by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya in the past.
The Buddha spoke again to Śāriputra:

"In the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, when women are pregnant and give birth, their bodies do not become exhausted, nor does their mind think of exhaustion; they think only of peace and security, and there is no suffering."
Furthermore, all those women therein shall likewise have no suffering, nor shall there be any foul odors or impurities.
Śāriputra, it is due to the power of the vows made by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya in the past that he has attained these wholesome dharmas; no other Buddha-field can equal his.

“Śāriputra! In the land of the Buddha Akṣobhya, there are no people who engage in farming for a livelihood, nor are there any who trade or travel back and forth; the people simply share in common joy, dwelling in stability and tranquil conduct.”
In that buddha-field, the people do not cling to craving or lust; they experience love and joy through natural causes and conditions.
When the wind rises in that land and blows upon the balustrades and trees, they produce sounds of lamentation.
Śāriputra! Even the most excellent sounds of the five musical tones cannot compare with the sound of the trees and stairways stirred by the wind in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya. Śāriputra!
"This is because he maintained the vows that the Tathāgata Akṣobhya made in the past when he was practicing the path of a Buddha.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"If there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to take up a purified and adorned buddha-field, they should take up that field by purifying it in accordance with the vows that Akṣobhya Buddha made in the past when he was practicing the bodhisattva path."
The Buddha spoke again to Śāriputra:
“In the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, there is no illumination from the light of the sun or moon, nor is there any place of deep darkness, nor is there any obstruction.”
Why is this so? Because the radiance of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, illuminates the entire trichiliocosm, remaining ever-luminous.

For example, suppose the Ghoṣila Monastery were firmly closed with its doors shut so that no wind could enter, and it were well-smeared with fine white plaster; if one were to place a maṇi jewel within it, that gem would illuminate it with its radiance, and all the people therein would receive its light day and night.
In this way, Śāriputra, the light of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya constantly illuminates the trichiliocosm.
Śāriputra! That which is called the Ghoṣavatī Monastery is the world Abhirati;
that which is the maṇi jewel is the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
The radiance of the maṇi jewel refers to the radiance of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya;
the people within the vihāra refer to the inhabitants of Akṣobhya’s buddha-field who dwell in peace and happiness.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“Wherever the Tathāgata Akṣobhya travels, beneath his footprints, golden lotuses with a thousand petals naturally spring forth from the earth.”
“Śāriputra! This is due to the vows made by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya when he was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, which have now reached their fulfillment.
The venerable Śāriputra asked the Buddha:
"When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, enters the palace hall, do thousand-petaled golden lotuses spontaneously arise?
Or do they spontaneously arise wherever he goes?"
The Buddha told the venerable Śāriputra:

"If the Tathāgata Akṣobhya enters a kingdom, a district, or a town, wherever he arrives, it shall be just as when he enters a palace or a hall; moreover, golden lotuses with a thousand petals will spontaneously arise."

If a son or daughter of good family intends that lotus flowers should naturally spring up beneath their feet as they enter the palace hall, those lotus flowers shall all gather together in one place and do so.
If they intend for them to rise up into the void, by the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha, and for the sake of the people, those lotus flowers shall ascend into the void and be arrayed in rows.
The Buddha spoke again to Śāriputra:

“That trichiliocosm is thus. If the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya were to dispatch an emanation to another world-system in a different direction, that [emanation] would also arise spontaneously—through the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority—the trichiliocosm would be adorned with lotuses of the seven treasures and golden hue.”
3. Chapter on the Disciples’ Accomplishment in Training. The Buddha spoke again to Śāriputra:

“When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya preaches the Dharma, within each instance of his preaching, there are incalculable and infinite numbers of people who follow the practice of the Vinaya, up to those who attain the realization of the path of Arhatship. Such assemblies of innumerable disciples, as well as those who have attained the eight stages of *dhyāna* (the eight liberations), are beyond calculation in the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.”
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“I do not see anyone who, by means of calculation or comparison, could count the number of those in this assembly.
They have cast off their heavy burdens, escaped from the prison, and are far removed from the *pātāla*, *aralāla*, *abhiṣa*, and *ayuta* hells. It is thus, Śāriputra!”
The assembly consists of incalculable numbers of good sons; these disciples possess immeasurable and incalculable wisdom, and they abide on the paths of srotāpanna, sakṛdāgāmin, anāgāmin, and arhat.
If one who is indolent attains the stage of *srotāpanna*, they are destined for seven births and seven deaths;
yet at the time this Dharma is preached, such a person fails to attain the superior maintenance required for those seven births and seven deaths.

"When Akṣobhya Tathāgata teaches the Dharma, those who attain realization of the path of the srotāpanna during his first teaching, those who attain realization of the path of the sakṛdāgāmin during his second teaching, those who attain realization of the path of the anāgāmin during his third teaching, and those who attain realization of the path of the arhat during his fourth teaching."
That buddha-field considers this good man to be indolent, because he does not sit in a single session to hear the Dharma and realize the path of an arhat.

In that field, a srotāpanna does not undergo seven more cycles of birth and death; rather, while practicing dhyāna among humans, he attains samādhi, and as a srotāpanna, he immediately realizes the path of an arhat through his own supernormal power.

In that land, the *srotāpanna* no longer returns to the world; having cast off all suffering, they attain *samādhi* therein, and as *sakṛdāgāmin*, they personally realize the path of an *arhat* through their own majestic spiritual power within that land.

In that land, the *anāgāmin* no longer ascends to be born among the *paranirmita-vaśavartin* devas, but instead personally realizes the path of an *arhat* through their own majestic spiritual power therein.
In that land, the *arhat* does not move up or down, but attains *parinirvāṇa* in the realm of *nirupadhiśeṣa-nirvāṇa* right there.
"In that land, the four paths of the śramaṇa are taught, leading thus until they attain the realization of the Way and abide therein. The Buddha said: "Śāriputra!"

If a son or daughter of good family attains mastery over the Dharma, they no longer lose their abiding in training, nor do they lose their training in other matters; thus, in the stage of non-training, they enter parinirvāṇa—the stage of non-training being the stage of the Arhat.

Śāriputra! This is how the disciples of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, achieve their training: there are none among them who establish themselves in coarse ways or remain in superior, preferred positions; these are the assembly of Arhats in the realm of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya—those whose cycle of birth and death has been severed, who have accomplished what was to be done, who have laid down the heavy burden through that which was to be performed, who have attained all that is to be attained, and who have utterly destroyed the affairs of the prison of toil and suffering through right and central understanding, further knowing the eight directions and the absence of dhyāna.
"Śāriputra, the arhat practices the eight directions without dhyāna;
this is the virtuous practice of the disciples in the realm of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, and it is the meritorious conduct resulting from the virtues of an arhat."
"The stairways of that land consist of the Three Jewels—first, gold; second, silver; and third, lapis lazuli—extending from the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven down to the Jambudvīpa continent."

When the gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven wish to go to the presence of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, they descend by this stairway. The gods of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven delight in making offerings to the people of the world below, saying:

"If one were to compare all that exists in our heaven with the people of the world below, everything in heaven is not as great as the world below, and furthermore, there is the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha."
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“The devas of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven delight in making offerings to the people of the world; however, if the people of the world were to ascend to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, they would no longer delight in making offerings to the devas of the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven.”

Why is this? It is because the Buddhas preach the sutras in my world; whatever exists in my world does not exist in that heavenly realm, nor is it like what exists in my world. In my world, there is the joy of making offerings to the Buddhas.

"The Trāyastriṃśa gods see the people of the world below, and the people of the world below see the palaces of the Trāyastriṃśa gods from afar, just as the people of this world see the palaces of the sun, moon, and stars from afar."
In this way, Śāriputra!

The people of that Buddha-field see from afar the celestial palaces of the gods as well as those who dwell among the desire-realm heavens; this is brought about by the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha. Such are the virtues and excellences possessed by the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
The Buddha spoke again to Śāriputra:
“In the trichiliocosm world-system of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya’s buddha-field, the Dharma is preached everywhere; the fourfold assembly of disciples fills the trichiliocosm without any vacancy.”
The disciples in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya do not think:
"What shall we eat today? Who will give us food today?"
Nor do they practice begging from house to house.
When the time arrives, the meal is spontaneously prepared; a full bowl appears naturally before them, and they take their food.
Once they have finished eating, the bowl vanishes spontaneously. Such is the manner of food and drink in that land.

The disciples no longer went out to seek robes or alms bowls; they did not cut cloth, nor sew clothes, nor wash clothes, nor dye clothes, nor make clothes, nor instruct others to make them. Through the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha, these things were produced naturally, and all dwelt together in peace and happiness.

“The Tathāgata Akṣobhya does not speak of the matter of offenses to his disciples—as I speak the fourteen points of the Dharma to my disciples—the Tathāgata Akṣobhya does not speak such teachings to his disciples.”
Why is this? Because in that land there are none who practice evil.
"Akṣobhya Buddha no longer bestows the precepts upon his disciples."

Why is this? Because in that buddha-field there are no people of short lifespan, nor are there any people who are obscured by evil; there are no kalpas of defilement, nor are there any fetters, nor any impurities. Seeing that field serves to eliminate all evils and defilements.
The Buddha spoke again to Śāriputra:
“When the Buddha Akṣobhya teaches the Dharma, his disciples immediately transcend their habitual desires. Why is this so?
Because they have already abandoned the evil realms, the disciples in that land never possess arrogance or conceit.
Unlike the disciples in this land who observe the precepts within the vihāras, there are no disciples in that land who act in such a manner.
Why is this so? Śāriputra, it is because the people possess the roots of goodness; therefore, the Dharma that is taught and the repentance they perform each find their proper place.
In that land, the matter of the five heinous crimes is not spoken of, for all have already severed every such transgression.

The disciples do not crave food or drink, nor do they crave robes or alms bowls, nor do they crave the desires of the multitude; they are free from attachment, and for them, only virtuous matters are taught.
Why is this? It is because they possess few desires and know contentment. "Śāriputra!..."
The Buddha Akṣobhya no longer bestows the precepts upon his disciples in the manner that I bestow them here upon my disciples. Why is this?
Because in his land there are no evil ones; these disciples take suffering, emptiness, impermanence, and non-self as their precepts.

In that land, there is also no such thing as receiving the precepts; it is like how the true sons of the Buddha (satpuruṣa) in this land shave off their hair and beards within my Dharma, possessing few desires and receiving my precepts.
Why is this? Because all the disciples in the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya gather together with sovereign ease, and there are no enemies or grudges. "Śāriputra!..."

In the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, the disciples do not practice collectively; rather, they practice the path alone and take no pleasure in communal practice, but simply cultivate all manner of virtues.
In that field, there is no one whose diligence is surpassed, nor can anyone who is indolent be seen.
“Śāriputra! This is the virtuous conduct of the disciples who have left the household life in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya preaches the Dharma for his disciples, the disciples do not look left or right, but listen to the sutra with single-minded attention. Among them, those who stand while listening to the sutra feel no physical exhaustion;
those who sit while listening to the sutra likewise feel no physical exhaustion, nor does their mind even think of exhaustion."

"When the Tathāgata Akṣobhya preaches the Dharma in mid-air, all his disciples listen to it; at that time, both those bhikṣus who have attained supernormal powers and those who have not, through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, all walk through the air while listening to the Dharma."
These disciples performed their practices in the air in three ways.
What are these three? First, standing; second, walking; and third, sitting.

Among them, there were those who attained parinirvāṇa while seated in the *paryaṅka* posture; when all their disciples likewise attained parinirvāṇa, the earth shook violently at that moment, and after they had passed into parinirvāṇa, devas and humans together made offerings to them.
Among them, there were Arhats who produced fire from within their own bodies to consume them and thus attained parinirvāṇa.
Among them, there were Arhats who, at the time of their parinirvāṇa, by means of their own meritorious conduct, moved as swiftly as a violent wind.
Among them, there are those who, like five-colored clouds moving through the sky, can no longer be known as to their location;
among them, there are disciples who, by virtue of their own merit, simply vanish away, no longer known as to their location—parinirvāṇa is thus.
Among them, there are those at the time of parinirvāṇa who release water from within their bodies in mid-air; that water does not fall to the ground but is extinguished and disappears.
That land is thus pure, causing the body to vanish and become unmanifest;
that land is thus pure, causing the body to vanish and become unmanifest as one enters parinirvāṇa.
The parinirvāṇa of the disciples is thus, Śāriputra!

This is because when the Tathāgata Akṣobhya—the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—was formerly practicing the bodhisattva path, he made vows which he maintained until he attained unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment; it is by means of these three modes that his disciples enter parinirvāṇa.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, among the disciples in the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya— those countless, incalculable disciples— there are few who are not fully endowed with the four analytical knowledges (*pratisaṃvid*), while many are fully endowed with them;
there are few disciples who do not attain the peaceful practice of the four bases of psychic power (*ṛddhipāda*), while many attain them."
“Śāriputra! These are the virtues accomplished by the disciples in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya.
The Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"In the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Akṣobhya, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, the practices of all his disciples are likewise infinite.
