Chapter Four: The Training of the Bodhisattvas.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra thought to himself:

“The Buddha has already explained the training for the accomplishment of the disciples; we pray that the Buddha will now further explain the training for the accomplishment of the bodhisattvas. Why is this?
It is because all must train to accomplish the illumination of these bodhisattvas.”
At that time, the Buddha, knowing the thoughts in the mind of the Venerable Śāriputra, addressed Śāriputra:

“In the buddha-field of that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Akṣobhya, there is such a great assembly of several hundreds of bodhisattvas, several thousands of bodhisattvas, several hundred million bodhisattvas, and several hundred thousand times ten million bodhisattvas.”
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“All the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have shaved their hair and beards in the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha do so entirely through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power; they all receive his Dharma teachings, recite them, and uphold them.”

The Dharma taught by me in this regard is but slight; the Dharma taught by the Buddha Akṣobhya is immeasurable and incalculable, such that compared to what I have taught, it exceeds my teaching a hundredfold, a thousandfold, ten-thousandfold, and even a hundred-millionfold beyond all calculation.
Śāriputra! This was the vow made by the Tathāgata Akṣobhya when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path:

"When I attain unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment as the most correct awakening, may all the bodhisattvas in my buddha-field, when I preach the Dharma, receive, recite, and uphold it all through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power."
The Buddha spoke again to Śāriputra:
“At that time, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, received the Dharma he had taught, recited it, and upheld it.”

These bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, having conceived the thought to travel from their own land to other worlds to go together to the presence of all Tathāgatas in order to hear the Dharma they preach, pay homage to those Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, recite it, and further inquire about its meaning for the sake of understanding; having paid homage to the Buddhas, recited the teachings, and inquired about their meaning, they then return once more to the place where Akṣobhya Tathāgata resides.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
"In this Bhadrakalpa, there shall be one thousand Buddhas; thus far, only four have passed.
A bodhisattva mahāsattva who wishes to see these Buddhas should aspire to be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya."

"If there are sons of good family or daughters of good family who, from this world or from other worlds, pass away and are reborn in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, those who have just been born shall immediately attain the stage of a disciple or a pratyekabuddha."

Why is this so? Those who, by means of causes and conditions, behold the Tathāgata and the Saṃgha, have severed the net of the malevolent Māra; they draw near to the stages of the disciples, the pratyekabuddhas, and the Buddhas, and shall attain unexcelled, perfect, true, and complete enlightenment. Such persons have thereby accomplished the state of a Tathāgata and have beheld the deeds of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

“Bodhisattvas who are born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya all abide in pure conduct; they practice all dharmas, they are masters of all dharmas, they dwell established in the Dharma, and they are immovable in the Buddha-way, further remaining firmly established in *avaivartika* (non-retrogression).”
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“If good sons or good daughters, having passed away from this world or from other worlds, go to those lands, such as these shall enter the abodes of the Buddhas.”

That Bodhisattva, having attained the awakening-mind, enters the state of fearlessness; the Bodhisattva unites with the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā), and wherever they may be, they accord with the same meaning, seeing the World-Honored One and knowing his dwelling place.
"In that buddha-field, those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are householders reside on high towers, while those who have left the home life to practice the Way do not dwell in houses.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"When the Buddha Akṣobhya preaches the Dharma, all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, receive his words of Dharma, recite them, and uphold them."

When those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have not left the household life do not see the Buddha face-to-face as he preaches the Dharma, they hear the words of the Dharma everywhere they sit through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power; having heard them, they immediately receive, recite, and uphold them.

When those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have left the household life see the Buddha preaching the Dharma face-to-face, and wherever they travel or sit, they likewise hear it all through the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power; having heard it, they immediately receive, recite, and uphold it.
After these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas pass away, they both continue to uphold the words of the Dharma, and wherever they are reborn in various buddha-fields, they maintain their mindfulness of them.
Śāriputra! This is the excellence of the Buddha Akṣobhya. Why is this so?
"As you have previously vowed, you shall naturally attain it.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"If there is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva of this world who wishes to see several hundreds of buddhas, several thousands of buddhas, several tens of thousands of buddhas, or several billions of nayutas of hundreds of thousands of buddhas, they should vow to be born in the land of Akṣobhya Buddha."

Bodhisattvas who have already been born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya shall see several hundreds of buddhas, several thousands of buddhas, several millions of buddhas, and several hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of buddhas. They shall plant various roots of virtue within that field; they shall preach the Dharma for countless hundreds of thousands of people, countless hundreds of thousands of millions of people, and countless hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of people, and they shall likewise cause them to plant roots of virtue.
The Buddha said: “Śāriputra!

If a bodhisattva mahāsattva, throughout this bhadrakalpa, were to provide offerings to all the Buddhas, the Gods among Gods—including robes, food and drink, bedding and seating, and medicines for the sick—and having done so, were then to leave the home life to study the Way, shaving off their hair and beard to become śramaṇas under all those Buddhas, the Gods among Gods;”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, if there were another bodhisattva mahāsattva who did not know that the merit obtained from practicing the *pāramitā* of gathering [beings] for a single lifetime in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya is greater,
what do you think? The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!"
This root of merit from the perfection of virtuous practices is a hundredfold, a thousandfold, ten-thousandfold, and even hundreds of billions of times greater;
it cannot be equaled. Śāriputra!
"This is the excellence and joy of the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"If a bodhisattva of this world or another world, at the end of his life, is reborn in the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya, all those who are about to be born there shall attain the stage of Avaivartika (non-retrogression)."
"Why is this? Because in that buddha-field, no malevolent māras appear before one, nor do malevolent māras harass people.
The Buddha said:

“Śāriputra! It is as if, for example, a person uses the power of incantations to cast spells against poison and spells against snakes; having removed their venom, they release them. The power of such a person is unsurpassable, for they rescue countless people from fear.”
That snake neither fears the person nor harms them; in this way, because that person has practiced the samādhi of dhyāna in previous lives, they extinguish the snake's venom through their own merit.
Thus it is, Śāriputra!

When Akṣobhya Buddha formerly sought the path of a bodhisattva, he practiced such vows and roots of virtue that he attained the way of the Buddha, eliminating the poison of the vexing Māras so that they no longer harass people.

"When Akṣobhya Buddha attained unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment and supreme awakening, the haughty Māras were no longer able to come and cause disturbance; nor could they disturb the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas or ordinary people; none of them were disturbed at all."
"Those people within the trichiliocosm who have likewise previously sat in this samādhi of tranquil concentration, through their own spiritual power (*sva-prabhāva*), are born into the Suyāma Heaven.

There, due to the extensive and universal practice of causes and conditions in former lives, they also employ the samādhi of causes and conditions, the stillness of their own spiritual power, and by means of these analogies, they preach the Dharma there."
When Suyāma heard this, having heard it, he immediately attained faith and joy, and came to make offerings to the disciples.
Suyāma said: "You have thus practiced non-attachment, known contentment, and cultivated your conduct in secluded places."
"In that land, the various Māras teach people to leave the household life and study the Way, no longer harassing others. Śāriputra!

This is the excellence and joy of the virtues of Akṣobhya Buddha’s land: at the first beat of the drum at night, he first takes pity on the people, desiring to bring about the deliverance of all bodhisattvas, as well as the disciples in training and ordinary persons, so that they may practice in peace, security, and tranquility."
The venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Indeed, O God among Gods!

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to fill a trichiliocosm with the seven treasures and offer them as a gift in order to be reborn in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, that person should not begrudge it; they should simply give it away.”
Why is this? Because that person will no longer fall back into the paths of the disciples or the pratyekabuddhas. Why is this?

That person shall immediately be established in the stage of non-retrogression; from one buddha-field to another buddha-field, they shall constantly behold all Buddhas with their own eyes, and shall fully recite and chant the practices of the Buddha-way. They shall attain the unsurpassed, right, and true path of supreme perfect enlightenment, and shall constantly behold hundreds of Buddhas, thousands of Buddhas, and hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of Buddhas, thereby accumulating the roots of virtue therein.
Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“O God among Gods!

For this reason, if a son of good family or a daughter of good family fills a trichiliocosm with the seven treasures and gives them as alms, thereby attaining rebirth in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, that person should give with joy and will then reach that buddha-field in peace and security.”
The Buddha said: "It is so, Śāriputra!
A bodhisattva mahāsattva attains birth in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya in safety."

For example, suppose there were a land of gold, free of gravel and stones and devoid of grass or trees, wherein there was purple-polished gold. A person would then take that gold, test it by smelting and refining it in fire, and fashion various objects from it for wear.

In this way, Śāriputra, the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya dwell in pure and subtle purity, gathered together in a pure assembly; such is the practice of these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

“Those who are born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, and those who are about to be born there, shall all be of one kind; their practice of the Way will be entirely equal, and all these bodhisattvas shall become Tathāgatas.”
Such a person, having transcended the stages of the disciples and the level of the pratyekabuddhas, is said to belong to the single path; there are no various heterodox or divergent paths.
A bodhisattva who wishes to attain this single path should aspire to be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.

“Śāriputra! This bodhisattva mahāsattva has attained the stage of *avaivartika* (non-retrogression) and has received the prediction (*vyākaraṇa*) from the Buddha Akṣobhya; therefore, I do not wish to send this bodhisattva mahāsattva to the presence of the Buddha Akṣobhya.”
For example, Śāriputra, suppose a wheel-turning monarch sends a messenger to the various minor kings, commanding them to bring the king’s precious treasures.
Upon hearing that the king has sent a messenger ordering the minor kings to come, they become distressed and weep because of the king’s precious treasures.

When the queen, the court ladies, and the crown prince heard that [the enemy] was using precious treasures as bait, they all feared the king; they then went to the city where the Great King resided, which had strong fortifications, and taking up residence within it, they found peace and security, no longer fearing the sight of their enemies or the suffering of famine.

"In this way, Śāriputra, I do not wish to send the bodhisattvas to the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha; it would be as if that king, for the sake of precious objects, were to cause his queens, court ladies, and crown prince equal distress."
One who seeks the path of a bodhisattva should regard themselves as a crown prince at a treasure site within a great king’s city, being free from fear and peril.
One should view the buddha-field of Akṣobhya as being like that great king; when the haughty Māra sees one seeking the path of a bodhisattva in this way, he will no longer cause disturbance.
"Just as a king’s frontier minister is difficult to overcome, so it is, Śāriputra!
Māra and his retinue of celestial officials cannot withstand the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha."
For example, suppose a person who is solitary, widowed, and fearful becomes afraid of an adversary; they then go to a city where they find peace, leaving the adversary helpless. Why is this so?
This person has already departed from opposition with others because they have attained a state of peace and security.

"In this way, Śāriputra, for those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, the path of Māra and the devas of Māra is severed; thus, the malevolent māras and the devas of Māra within the trichiliocosm no longer harass those seeking the bodhisattva path, nor those on the path of the disciples, nor the buddha-field of Akṣobhya. Māra and the devas of Māra no longer initiate demonic deeds, nor do they cause further harassment."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
If there are bodhisattvas who are born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya—those who are about to be born—their persons will no longer be harassed by the māras or the devas."
Why is this? Because in the past, when Akṣobhya Buddha was practicing the bodhisattva path, he made this vow as the root of his merit:

"When I attain unsurpassed, perfect, true enlightenment and become a most perfectly awakened one, let there be no Māras or celestial Māras in my buddha-field who can initiate demonic deeds or cause disturbance."
"Just as when a person who has drunk poison drinks an antidote, the food and drink are digested and the poison no longer circulates.
It is thus, Śāriputra, because of their equal vows."

In the past, Akṣobhya Buddha made such vows as the roots of virtue that, even unto his buddha-field, no Māras or Māra-sons shall again raise disturbances or cause turmoil; such are the qualities possessed by that buddha-field.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra thought to himself:
"I wish to behold that buddha-field, as well as the Buddha Akṣobhya and his disciples."

Thereupon, the Buddha, knowing the thoughts in Śāriputra’s mind, immediately caused him to enter a samādhi of miraculous power corresponding to that very form. By the power bestowed by the Buddha, the Venerable Śāriputra, while remaining in his seat, beheld the buddha-field of Akṣobhya as well as his disciples and others.
At that time, the Buddha said to Śāriputra:
"Do you see Akṣobhya Buddha, his disciples, and his buddha-field? He replied:
“Yes, indeed, I see them, O God among Gods! ‘How so, Śāriputra?’”
"According to what you understand, is there anything superior to the gods and humans in the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya?
Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
"O God among Gods!"
I no longer know of any city or fortress that could surpass it.
In that land, among the devas and the people, there are no heterodox paths; there is only the true path, and they take supreme delight in one another.

Why is this? I see that in those buddha-fields, all beings enjoy delightful food and drink made of celestial substances and take pleasure in one another; at their center sits Akṣobhya Buddha, teaching the Dharma to all his disciples.
“Just as, O God among Gods!
a person standing in the middle of the great ocean cannot see the limits of the mountains and trees in the east, nor can they see the limits of the trees in the south, west, or north.”
Thus it is, O God among Gods!
It is impossible to find the eastern limit of the disciples in the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya, nor can one find its limits in the south, west, or north.
Contemplating the Dharma in this manner, his body remained unmoved;
O God among Gods!
Through such contemplative concentration, his body became entirely motionless.
The disciples in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya listen to the Dharma with their bodies unmoving and seated in meditative concentration;
they listen to the Dharma in such a way that their bodies likewise do not move.

"If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to fill this trichiliocosm with the seven treasures and, having offered them as a gift, thereby attain birth in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, one should give with joy; such a person shall then attain peaceful birth among the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya."
Why is this? Because such a person has thus attained the state of an avaivartika.
It is, O Devātideva, as if...
Suppose there is a person who carries a royal letter and provisions, having sealed the letter with the king’s seal, and travels to another country.
As this person proceeds through the districts and towns of that foreign land, there is no one on the road to kill him, nor anyone able to harass him; he goes and returns alone without any trouble.
The Buddha said, “It is so, Śāriputra!

Those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, and those who are about to be born—those who pass away from this world or from worlds in other directions to be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya—all attain the stage of non-retrogression (avaivartika) and immediately behold the unsurpassed, right, and true path. They travel from one buddha-field to another, reciting and chanting the matters of the Buddha-way, always delighting in the Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, until they achieve unsurpassed, right, and true enlightenment, the most perfect awakening.”
Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“O God among Gods!
Those here who have attained the path of a srotāpanna and those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya are exactly equal.”
Why is this? Because the stream-enterer (srotāpanna), having severed the evil paths, abides on the track of the Way.
Thus it is, O God among Gods!

If there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have been born, or are about to be born, in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya Buddha, these persons shall all manifest the severance of the evil paths and no longer abide in the stages of the śrāvakas or pratyekabuddhas. They shall travel from one buddha-field to another, taking delight in the Buddhas—the Gods among Gods—and their disciples, until they achieve unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment as the most supreme awakening.
The Buddha said: “It is so, Śāriputra!

If there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from this world or from other worlds, pass away and are reborn in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, they do so by having already transcended the stages of the śrāvaka and pratyekabuddha. From one buddha-field they travel to another buddha-field, everywhere reciting the deeds of the Buddhas’ path and personally beholding all the Tathāgatas, until they attain unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment.”
For example, Śāriputra, just as a stream-enterer has crossed over from heterodox paths and evil dharmas, and there is no difference in their attainment of the Way; so it is, Śāriputra.

If there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from this world or from other worlds, pass away and are reborn in the land of Akṣobhya Buddha, or those who are about to be so reborn, they shall all no longer be separated from the unsurpassed, right, and true path. From one buddha-field they shall travel to another buddha-field, reciting the deeds of the Buddhas, always delighting in the unsurpassed, right, and true path of the Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, until they attain the unsurpassed, right, and true path of supreme perfect enlightenment.
The venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“O God among Gods!
Is it that those who dwell here on the stage of the once-returner (sakṛdāgāmin) and those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya are exactly the same?”
"O God among Gods!
Are those Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya Buddha equal to those Anāgāmins who dwell in the stage of no-return?"
"O God among Gods!
Are those Arhats who dwell on the stage of non-attachment, and those Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, equal to one another?"
The Buddha addressed the venerable Śāriputra, saying: "Do not speak such words. Why is this?"
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas here who receive the prediction of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment, and those bodhisattvas born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, are exactly like this.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
The bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who sit beneath the Bodhi tree here are just like those bodhisattvas born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya. Why is this so?

Śāriputra! For the sake of manifesting the Tathāgata, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva cannot be shaken by the Māras of oppression; he transcends the stages of the Śrāvakas and Pratyekabuddhas, travels from one Buddha-field to another, and always follows the instructions and commands of all Buddhas until he attains unsurpassed, perfect, true, and supreme enlightenment.
At that time, Ānanda thought to himself:
"I wish to test Subhūti to see what he will say in response to me.
Then the Venerable Ānanda asked the Venerable Subhūti:
"Venerable Subhūti! Do you see the Buddha Akṣobhya, his disciples, and his buddha-field?
Subhūti then said to Ānanda:
“Look upward. Ānanda replied, “Venerable Subhūti!”
"I have looked upward, and what is above is entirely empty space. Subhūti said to Ānanda:
"Just as you, Venerable One, see emptiness when looking upward, so too should one contemplate Akṣobhya Buddha, his disciples, and his buddha-field."
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked:
"As it has been taught by the God among Gods,
those bodhisattva-mahāsattvas here who receive their prediction and those bodhisattvas who are born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya are indeed equal."
"O God among Gods!
By what reason are they equal and identical?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

"By means of the application [of the Dharma] and so forth, they are equal. 5. Chapter on the Parinirvāṇa of the Buddha. *The Sūtra of the Land of Akṣobhya Buddha*, Chapter Five: The Parinirvāṇa of the Buddha. At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra thought to himself:

"The Buddha has already spoken of the virtuous names [attained] by Akṣobhya Buddha when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path; he has further spoken of the excellence and joy of that buddha-field; and he has also spoken of the vows and accomplishments learned by the disciples and bodhisattvas. The Buddha should now further speak of what kind of spiritual responses occurred at the time of Akṣobhya Buddha’s Great Parinirvāṇa."
"O God among Gods!
Thereupon, the Buddha, knowing the thoughts in Śāriputra’s mind, addressed Śāriputra, saying:

"On the day of the Great Parinirvāṇa of the Buddha Akṣobhya, throughout all the provinces and kingdoms of the trichiliocosm, transformation-bodies will manifest and preach the Dharma—the teachings they shall deliver being just like those previously taught. At that time, the people will again practice the path of the Arhat; they will no longer fluctuate between higher or lower states, but shall be established in the fruit of Arhatship."

"When Akṣobhya Buddha enters parinirvāṇa, there shall be a bodhisattva mahāsattva named Saugandhahasta; he shall receive the prediction of enlightenment, and his name shall be Kṣemaṃkara-padmapuṣpa—translated into Chinese as Suvarṇavarṇa-padma Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

All the excellence and well-being found in the buddha-field of the Buddha Suvarṇapuṣpa shall likewise be as the excellence and well-being found in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya; all the disciples of the Buddha Suvarṇapuṣpa shall likewise be like those of Akṣobhya."

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Buddha Akṣobhya enters parinirvāṇa, there shall be a great trembling that pervades the entire trichiliocosm; the sound shall be heard as far up as the Akaniṣṭha Heaven, from the Ābhāsvara Heaven upward.
When the Buddha Akṣobhya enters parinirvāṇa, such a portentous response shall occur."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!
All the excellent medicinal herbs and trees in the Buddha-field of Akṣobhya bend toward where Akṣobhya Buddha entered parinirvāṇa to pay him homage."

"When the Buddha Akṣobhya enters the Great Parinirvāṇa, the devas and humans shall hold flowers, incense, blended perfumes, and powdered incense to offer as worship, scattering them upon his body. Having made these offerings, the flowers, blended perfumes, powdered incense, and other jewels held by those devas and humans will extend upward to the void for forty *li*, forming a circular flower-canopy."
"When the Buddha Akṣobhya enters the great parinirvāṇa, all the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas of this trichiliocosm will turn toward him."
"When Akṣobhya Buddha enters mahāparinirvāṇa, these people and the devas—through the power of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority—all behold Akṣobhya Buddha entering mahāparinirvāṇa."
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Buddha Akṣobhya enters mahāparinirvāṇa, the devas and human beings will constantly grieve day and night, saying:
'The parinirvāṇa of the Buddha Akṣobhya has come too swiftly; he has perished for us.'"
The people, no longer able to enjoy their pleasures or obtain what they desired, became sorrowful and anxious in mind, saying:
"The Buddha Akṣobhya has entered parinirvāṇa too soon; we have lost the peace and security of the people."
His mind was filled with sorrow and he said,
"The eyes of the world are lost.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

"If there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from this world or from worlds in other directions, pass away and are reborn in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya—whether they have already been born there or are about to be born—all such persons shall receive the prediction of enlightenment (*vyākaraṇa*). They shall travel together with their peers from one region to another, traveling in groups of several hundreds or thousands; these bodhisattva-mahāsattvas shall see several hundreds of thousands of Tathāgatas, shall see countless Buddhas, and shall see countless forms of omniscience (*sarvajñatā*)."

"If there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who, from this world or from worlds in other directions, pass away and are reborn in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, or those who are about to be reborn there, such persons shall also travel together with the assembly; by means of the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power and for the sake of sarvajñā (all-knowledge), they shall become avaivartika (non-retrogressive)."
“Bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who hear this Dharma-sūtra of the name of the Buddha Akṣobhya will all be freed from the net of Māra.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!”

When the Buddha Akṣobhya enters mahāparinirvāṇa, those who abide in the practice of the Dharma and all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who are born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya shall likewise travel together with their peers, seeking out the former vows of the Buddha Akṣobhya, and thereafter they shall be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.
The bodhisattva-mahāsattva shall then recite eight hundred gates; having recited them, he shall recite all dharmas, and thereupon there will be the supreme and subtle buddha-field of Akṣobhya.
All bodhisattva-mahāsattvas attain eight hundred gateways of mindfulness for walking and dwelling:
"I shall be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.

They should also recite these eight hundred gateways; having recited them, they should further recite all dharmas and perceive the sublime phrases, thus correctly receiving and upholding them, such bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.

“The teaching of the Buddha Akṣobhya when he is currently present and at the time of his parinirvāṇa is equal and without difference; the buddha-field is identical to that manifested by the Tathāgata—from the stage of non-retrogression until the attainment of unsurpassed, perfect, true, and complete enlightenment.”

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, fire spontaneously issues from within the body of Akṣobhya Buddha; having burned his own body, it becomes golden in color, then shatters like mustard seeds and does not reassemble again. Once this is finished, he is naturally reborn."
For example, Śāriputra, there is a tree named Timira; even if its hair-like fibers are cut into segments until they are no longer visible, it naturally grows back.
In the same way, Śāriputra!
"When the Buddha Akṣobhya enters Mahāparinirvāṇa, his body will be broken and no longer visible, yet it will naturally manifest again. Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
When the Buddha Akṣobhya enters mahāparinirvāṇa, his physical remains and the places where he sat will appear spontaneously.
It is like a mountain: though that mountain may be shattered and no longer visible, it spontaneously returns to its original place.

In this way, Śāriputra, when the Buddha Akṣobhya enters mahāparinirvāṇa, his bones will spontaneously break apart; his skeletal remains will no longer be seen, returning instead to their natural state.

At that time, all the people of the trichiliocosm shall make offerings to his body by constructing stūpas of the seven precious gems; this trichiliocosm shall be adorned with those stūpas of the seven precious gems and with golden lotuses.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas of the buddha-field of Akṣobhya perform prostrations, such a portentous sign occurs: various jewels spontaneously appear and remain before them."
“Any bodhisattva-mahāsattva who is born into the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, or who is about to be born there, shall see the Buddha’s mind as undisturbed;
at the time of their passing away, all devas and humans shall make offerings to their bodies.”

While the devas and human beings aspire to initiate offerings for his body, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva, by virtue of his own merit, travels swiftly through space until they no longer know his whereabouts at all.

For example, Śāriputra, it is like taking grass and wood and placing them in a fire so that they smolder and emit smoke; that smoke rises into the void, moves through the void, and is completely extinguished within the void, such that its destination cannot be known.
Such is the dharma-body of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in those buddha-fields.

"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the lifespan of a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya comes to an end and he is approaching death, he sees other bodhisattva mahāsattvas sitting beneath the tree of enlightenment in other world-systems. These are the auspicious signs at the time of his passing: he further sees other bodhisattvas entering their mothers’ wombs; he also sees other bodhisattva mahāsattvas being born from their mothers’ right sides, taking seven steps, and enjoying themselves among the court ladies; he sees other bodhisattva mahāsattvas leaving home to study the Way; he sees other bodhisattvas sitting beneath the tree of enlightenment, subduing Māra, and attaining the wisdom of omniscience (sarvajñājñāna); and he sees the Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, turning the wheel of Dharma in other world-systems."
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!
When the bodhisattvas in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya are approaching the end of their lives, there are such spontaneous auspicious omens as these.”
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, when the Buddha Akṣobhya enters parinirvāṇa, the Dharma taught by that Buddha shall remain for several hundreds of thousands of kalpas."
The venerable Śāriputra asked the Buddha:
“O God among Gods!
By what reckoning does the Dharma taught by the Buddha remain for a hundred thousand kalpas?”
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
"Twenty small kalpas constitute one kalpa; this is the number of kalpas for which the Dharma taught by the Buddha shall remain for hundreds of thousands of kalpas.
Furthermore, Śāriputra!"
When this Dharma is extinguished, the entire trichiliocosm shall be greatly illuminated and its earth shall tremble violently.
This Dharma is not extinguished by the malevolent Māras or the devas of Māra’s realm, nor is it extinguished by the disciples of the Devātideva.

The bhikṣus gradually took pleasure in seclusion and frequented it; having gradually become secluded and frequenting it together, they practiced in unison and no longer listened extensively to the Dharma.

Having ceased to listen, they no longer applied themselves with great diligence, nor did they attain great vigor; thus, even the Dharma-preacher bhikṣu became secluded regarding the teaching of the Dharma.
"Because the teaching of the Dharma is meager, for this reason the Dharma will gradually perish and eventually cease to be seen.
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra asked the Buddha,
"How is it so, O God among Gods?"
“By what kind of virtuous conduct does a bodhisattva mahāsattva attain rebirth in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya?
The Buddha told Śāriputra:
“This bodhisattva mahāsattva should study the practices of Akṣobhya when he formerly sought the bodhisattva path, and should give rise to such a vow and intention:”
"May I be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.
It is by practicing in this way that bodhisattva-mahāsattvas are able to be born in that buddha-field.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

When a bodhisattva practices the perfection of giving, accumulates the roots of virtue, and maintains the vow for unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment, they shall come to be in the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha;
it is by means of such practice that a bodhisattva mahāsattva attains birth in that buddha-field.
The Bodhisattva’s practice of the precepts of the *pāramitā* consists in upholding the vow for the unsurpassed, right, and true path, whereby one comes to dwell beside the Buddha Akṣobhya;
it is by means of such practice that a Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva attains rebirth in that Buddha-field.
When a bodhisattva practices the perfection of patience and maintains the vow for supreme, true, and correct enlightenment, they will be able to dwell in the presence of the Buddha Akṣobhya;
it is by practicing in this way that a bodhisattva-mahāsattva attains rebirth in that buddha-field.
The Bodhisattva practices the perfection of vigor and maintains the vow for unsurpassed, true, and correct enlightenment, thereby attaining birth in the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha;
it is by means of this practice that the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to be born in the land of Akṣobhya Buddha.
The Bodhisattva practices the perfection of single-mindedness, upholding the vow for the unsurpassed, true, and correct path, and thus attains birth in the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha;
it is by means of this practice that the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva is able to be born in that Buddha-field.
When a bodhisattva practices the perfection of wisdom and maintains the vow for the unsurpassed, right, and true path, they will come to be in the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha;
it is by means of this that a bodhisattva mahāsattva is able to be born in that buddha-field.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra, [the bodhisattva] thinks:

'The radiance of the Buddha Akṣobhya illuminates the entire trichiliocosm; I shall vow to behold this, and having beheld it, may I attain unexcelled, perfect, true, and complete enlightenment, and may I, in turn, illuminate my own buddha-field with such radiance.'"
“By practicing in this way, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva attains birth in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.

‘When I behold the countless, incalculable disciples in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, having seen them, I too shall practice in such a manner that when I realize unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment as a Most Rightly Awakened One, there shall be countless disciples.’”
“By practicing in this way, the bodhisattva mahāsattva attains birth in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.

‘In the buddha-field of Akṣobhya there are several hundreds of bodhisattvas, several thousands of bodhisattvas, and several hundreds of thousands of bodhisattvas; I shall behold these venerable bodhisattvas in their silent meditative practices, and I shall train in them.’”
One should clearly understand and know this in every respect: "I shall be no different from my fellow students; I shall dwell together with those of such a kind."

Desiring to be fully endowed with great loving-kindness and great compassion for the sake of the Buddha and the meaning of the śramaṇa, one should be without the state of a pratyekabuddha, without the conduct of a disciple, without the mind of a disciple, and without the mind of a solitary realizer (pratyekabuddha). One should dwell truthfully in emptiness, free from the dharmas of the evil realms, and constantly keep in mind the names of all Buddhas, the names of all Tathāgatas, the name of Sarvajñā (omniscience), the names of all dharmas, and the names of the Saṃgha—just as all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas do.

"If even good sons and good daughters who merely hear the name can attain birth in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, how much more so those who practice all the perfections (pāramitās), cultivate roots of goodness, and maintain vows to be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya?"

Once one has accumulated these roots of goodness, one will immediately attain unsurpassed, perfect, true enlightenment; how much more so when one accumulates the roots of goodness of all the various *pāramitās*, by which one will be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya?
By practicing in this manner, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are able to be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.

Furthermore, Śāriputra, a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who wishes to be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya should contemplate the causes and conditions of the countless Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, such as the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka* (Flower Garland of the True Dharma) and others; he should contemplate the teachings spoken by those Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, and reflect that there is none equal to them.
"May I attain the Unsurpassed, Right, and True Path of Supreme Enlightenment, and may I preach the Dharma in this same way.

Just as the Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, have considered the causes and conditions of their various disciples, so too, when I attain the Unsurpassed, Right, and True Path of Supreme Enlightenment, shall I likewise have an infinite and incalculable assembly of disciples."
“Śāriputra! If there are good sons or good daughters who should keep these three matters in mind, they should clearly understand and keep these three great matters in mind.

If good sons or good daughters, by means of keeping these three great matters in mind, combine them with the roots of merit to create traces for all sentient beings through mindfulness, upholding, and vows, and to establish the unsurpassed, right, and true path—doing so because of all sentient beings—they vow to these three matters.”

“Good son, good daughter, bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who aspire to unexcelled, perfect, and true enlightenment cannot be limited by all sentient beings. Suppose someone were to come with a vessel, wishing to measure out space, and having arrived, said: ‘Good son!’”
"Take these roots of goodness and share them with me. The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!"

Śāriputra, if these roots of goodness possessed form, all sentient beings could take them up with vessels until their limits were reached; yet space would never come to an end. Such is the manner in which these roots of goodness may be taken up with vessels. Śāriputra!

One vows that the roots of goodness shall be directed toward unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment; this, moreover, cannot be grasped by means of a vessel—this is what is called the root of goodness of *sarvajñatā* (all-knowledge).
If one contemplates these three roots of goodness, one will immediately attain the Three Jewels;
if there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who contemplates these three roots of goodness, they vow that all shall behold wholesome dharmas.

When a bodhisattva practices these three matters—the roots of goodness and vows—they subdue all Māras and their retinues. Whatever Buddha-field they desire to be born in, they shall immediately be born there—whether it be in the south, the west, the north, the zenith, or the nadir, and likewise in the four intermediate directions.

"If there is a bodhisattva-mahāsattva who, recollecting these three matters, accumulates roots of goodness and maintains them as an act of dedication, and having performed this dedication, directs his vow toward the buddha-field of Akṣobhya, that person shall immediately be reborn in that buddha-field."
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“Whether it be several hundred buddha-fields, several thousand buddha-fields, or several hundred thousand buddha-fields—the excellence and joy of such buddha-fields are empty; the buddha-field of Akṣobhya is likewise.”
"I shall behold the excellence and bliss of that Buddha-field; having seen it, I too shall take it up.

In this manner, through such excellence and bliss of a Buddha-field, I shall encourage and assist several hundred bodhisattvas, several thousand bodhisattvas, and several hundred thousand bodhisattvas, manifesting it to them so as to cause them to rejoice and leap with joy, reaching up to the World-Honored One Akṣobhya."
"By practicing in this way, Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas are born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.

If there is a Bodhisattva Mahāsattva who single-mindedly generates this intention toward Akṣobhya Buddha, yet fails to act accordingly, such a person would be a deceiver; however, by simply generating this intention single-mindedly, one shall be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya."
"It is, for example, like a city that has no marketplace, no gardens, no bathing pools, and no goods; it has neither elephants nor horses, nor anyone who comes or goes within it."
"What do you think, Śāriputra!
Would there be a powerful king residing within that city?
With such inferior merit as that city possesses, would it not be miserable?"
"A powerful king resides in a great city; that city possesses the myriad things of virtuous excellence, and thus such a city is the most supreme. It is even so, Śāriputra!"

"In this regard, the excellence and joy of my Buddha-field within this trichiliocosm are such that, compared to my own Buddha-field, they are inferior; they do not possess the same superior excellence. Such is the excellence and joy found here in my Buddha-field."

Śāriputra! If a bodhisattva wishes to purify the excellence of his buddha-field and wishes to take it up, he should purify and take it up in this manner, just as Akṣobhya Buddha took up the excellence of his purified buddha-field when he formerly practiced the bodhisattva path.
"Furthermore, Śāriputra!

Having attained supreme, perfect, and true enlightenment, he causes people to abide in the path of the srotāpanna, the sakṛdāgāmin, the anāgāmin, and the arhat; furthermore, he teaches and leads them to abide in the path of the pratyekabuddha."

All my disciples and other disciples shall assemble together, yet they will not equal even a hundredfold, a thousandfold, ten-thousandfold, a hundred-thousand-billionfold, or a myriad-billionfold the assembly of disciples in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya; this is so except for the fact that there is no difference in their teaching of liberation.

My disciples, as well as all the disciples of Maitreya Buddha and the disciples of others, shall all assemble together; yet even when combined, they will not equal even a hundredth, a thousandth, a ten-thousandth, or a hundred-millionth part of the assembly of disciples in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.
"Why is this? Because whenever the Buddha Akṣobhya preaches the Dharma, the number of people who attain the Way cannot be calculated.
The Buddha said:

“Śāriputra! Setting aside my own disciples, and further setting aside the disciples of Maitreya Buddha; even if one were to gather together all the disciples of the Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, throughout the Bhadrakalpa, along with all other disciples who have attained the Way, they would not equal even a hundredth, a thousandth, a ten-thousandth, a hundred-millionth, or a trillionth part of the assembly of disciples in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya Buddha. This is because those who speak of liberation are none other than these very people.”
At that time, the Venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“According to what has been spoken by the God among Gods, and as I understand it, one should regard that buddha-field as a field of arhats, not a field of ordinary worldlings.”
"Why is that? Because those Arhats are exceedingly numerous.
The Buddha said:
"In this way, Śāriputra, the arhats in that land— those for whom birth and death have been exhausted— are exceedingly numerous.

Just as all the stars within a trichiliocosm cannot be counted and their number cannot be known, so too the number of those who attain arhatship whenever Akṣobhya Buddha preaches the Dharma cannot be counted."
In this way, Śāriputra, at each and every assembly,
incalculable and infinite numbers of people attained the path of arhatship.
One might be able to count the number of stars within the trichiliocosm.

The gods and people of Akṣobhya Buddha’s land perceive his radiance with their divine eyes due to the accumulation of roots of merit. Within this trichiliocosm of Akṣobhya Buddha’s land, these sons and daughters of good family go day and night to the presence of Akṣobhya Buddha.
Śāriputra, if there are those who hear this Dharma-sūtra of the meritorious names, and having heard it, immediately receive, uphold, and recite it,
these good men and good women have all previously heard and seen the Buddha Akṣobhya when he was formerly seeking the bodhisattva path.
Why is this? Because if there are those who hear this *Dharmaparyāya* of the Meritorious Names of that Buddha and immediately develop faith,

they will all receive, recite, uphold, and proclaim this *Dharmaparyāya* of the Meritorious Names of the Buddha Akṣobhya throughout the buddha-fields of the ten directions— whether they are persons seeking the path of a bodhisattva or seeking the path of a disciple.

Furthermore, the irreversible bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling in other buddha-fields, as well as other bodhisattvas, also proclaim the vows made by Akṣobhya Buddha, as well as those who have been born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya and those who are yet to be born. It is the same in the east; it is likewise in the south, the west, the north, the zenith, the nadir, and throughout the ten directions.

"In all Buddha-fields, those who seek the path of a bodhisattva shall all receive this Dharma-sūtra of the Virtuous Name, recite it, uphold it, and explain it; they shall abide as *avaivartika* bodhisattva-mahāsattvas and further achieve unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment.
This applies equally to other bodhisattvas who have made vows under Akṣobhya Buddha, those already born in his Buddha-field, and those who are yet to be born."
“In this way, Śāriputra, the Buddha Akṣobhya dwells in the world Abhirati, radiantly illuminating all those throughout the ten directions who seek the path of a bodhisattva.”

"If there are good sons or good daughters who recite the *Dharmaparyāya on the Virtuous Names of Akṣobhya Buddha*, and having heard it, immediately uphold, recite, and vow to be born in the land of Akṣobhya Buddha, then at the time of their passing, Akṣobhya Buddha will immediately keep that person in mind."

Why is this? Should malevolent Māras find an opportunity to cause them to turn back from their vows, the Tathāgata will take them into consideration; thus, those good men and good women shall no longer turn back, and they will surely attain their vows as well as unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment.
If there should be other external causes or conditions, none would be able to afflict or harm them.
In this way, fire, swords, poison, and water likewise have no effect upon them;
even if there should be those who strike or beat them, they likewise do not turn toward [the assailants].
Furthermore, they shall not fear humans or non-humans; being thus protected by those who hold such views, they will be reborn in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya.
The Buddha said:
"Śāriputra, it is just as if..."
Just as the sun palace dwells afar yet its radiant heat shines upon the people of the world from a distance;
so too does the Buddha Akṣobhya dwell afar, yet his radiance shines upon all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling in other worlds.
“Just as a bhikṣu who has attained the divine eye, while staying at a distance, sees the light of forms from afar;
so too, Śāriputra, Akṣobhya Buddha,
while staying at a distance, sees the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas dwelling in other world-systems, seeing their complexions and physical forms.”
"Just as a bhikṣu with supernormal powers, dwelling at a distance, knows the thoughts in the minds of others;
so too, Śāriputra, the Buddha Akṣobhya,
dwelling at a distance, knows from afar the thoughts of all the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas residing in other world-systems."
“Śāriputra, it is just as a bhikṣu possessing supernormal powers, dwelling at a distance, hears sounds from afar with his divine ear;
in the same way, Śāriputra,

the Buddha Akṣobhya, dwelling at a distance, hears from afar the speech of the bodhisattva-mahāsattvas in other world-systems and those born in his land— this Tathāgata Akṣobhya knows the names and clans of these good sons and good daughters.”
“Śāriputra, if there are those who receive, recite, and uphold this Dharma-sūtra of the title ‘The Merits,’ such persons shall be regarded as having seen the Buddha Akṣobhya;
you should know that when such persons approach the end of their lives, the Buddha Akṣobhya will immediately appear before them.”
The worthy Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“It is difficult to encounter, O God among Gods!
The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, have truly entrusted all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas with this charge.”
The Buddha said, “It is so, Śāriputra! The Buddhas,
the Gods among Gods, earnestly entrust all bodhisattva-mahāsattvas.”
Why is this? Because when a bodhisattva truly accepts an entrustment, they have already truly accepted all sentient beings.

It is, for example, like a wheel-turning monarch who possesses first, second, third, fourth, fifth, tenth, and twentieth storehouses—indeed, incalculable granaries—containing rice, barley, wheat, and various other grains; when grain becomes expensive, he opens them to make the grain cheap.
In this way, Śāriputra,
when a Bodhisattva has received the prediction from a Tathāgata but has not yet attained supreme perfect enlightenment, it is like a time of high grain prices;
once he has attained unsurpassed, true, and complete awakening, he then teaches the Dharma with peace and security, as if grain were cheap.
"For this reason, the Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, earnestly entrust [this teaching] to the Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas. The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!"

If there is a bodhisattva mahāsattva who, upon hearing this *Dharmaparyāya on the Meritorious Names of Akṣobhya Buddha*, receives, recites, and upholds it as soon as they have heard it—even if they do not vow to be born in the buddha-field of Akṣobhya—it should be known that this bodhisattva mahāsattva is comparable to one who is irreversible (*avaivartika*).

"If there should be a bodhisattva mahāsattva who receives this *Dharmaparyāya on the Meritorious Names of Akṣobhya Buddha*, and having received it, upholds, recites, and explains it for several hundred people, several hundreds of millions, or hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of people, they shall cause those hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of people to accumulate roots of merit."
According to the roots of merit this person has accumulated, those roots of merit of that bodhisattva are incalculable;
because the roots of merit of this bodhisattva-mahāsattva are so numerous, he shall immediately sit upon the seat of unsurpassed, perfect, and true enlightenment.
The Buddha said, “Śāriputra!

If there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to swiftly attain unexcelled, perfect, true, and complete enlightenment, they should receive this Dharma-sūtra of the Virtuous Name, uphold it, and recite it.”

Having received, upheld, and recited it, they explain it to several hundreds, several thousands, or several hundreds of thousands of people; then, by reflecting upon the matters as they have been explained, they immediately attain great wisdom, and their transgressions are thereby extinguished.
Having attained this great wisdom and having extinguished their transgressions, those individuals, through their own merit, bring the path of birth and death to an end.
The Buddha told Śāriputra:

“If there are good men or good women who seek the path of the disciples, upon hearing this *Dharmaparyāya of the Dharma-Text on the Virtuous Names of Akṣobhya Buddha*, they should immediately receive and uphold it, and they should recite it from memory.
Having received, upheld, and recited it from memory, they shall explain it for several hundreds, several thousands, or several hundreds of thousands of people.”
"If there are good sons or good daughters who receive this Dharma-sūtra, they shall, by their own merit, personally realize the fruit of Arhatship.
The Buddha said, "Śāriputra!"

If there are good sons or good daughters who single-mindedly uphold and recite this Dharma-sūtra of the Meritorious Names, such persons shall thus set aside the state of Perfect Enlightenment and, by means of their own merit, realize the fruit of Arhatship.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“This *Dharmaparyāya on the Meritorious Names of Akṣobhya Buddha* shall never fall into the hands of the foolish; it shall instead fall into the hands of the wise.”
The Buddha said,
“Śāriputra! Those sons and daughters of good family into whose hands this Dharma discourse titled ‘The Designation of Virtues’ comes shall be considered as having already seen the Tathāgata.”
For example, Śāriputra, suppose there are various kinds of jewels of immense value that have been gathered from the great ocean. What do you think, Śāriputra?
"If one were to gather various kinds of jewels from the great ocean, in whose hands would they first arrive?
Śāriputra replied, "O God among Gods!"
"It should first be placed into the hands of the king, or the crown prince,
or those around him. The Buddha said, "So it is, Śāriputra!"
"This *Dharmaparyāya on the Meritorious Names of Akṣobhya Buddha* shall first reach the hands of Bodhisattvas and those who are non-regressive (avaivartika). Furthermore, Śāriputra!"

When a bodhisattva-mahāsattva hears this *Dharmaparyāya on the Meritorious Names of Akṣobhya Buddha*, and upon hearing it, receives, upholds, and recites it, having recited it, they shall immediately and exclusively accomplish the unsurpassed, right, and true path of supreme perfect enlightenment.
The venerable Śāriputra addressed the Buddha, saying:
“This *Dharmaparyāya on the Meritorious Names of the Buddha Akṣobhya* shall never be heard, received, upheld, or recited by those of meager merit.”
Why is this so? O God among Gods!
It is because they are unable to attain the stage of *avaivartika*.
The Buddha told the venerable Śāriputra: "It is truly so.
If there were a son of good family or a daughter of good family who filled this entire world with gold and silver and gave it as a gift, making this aspiration:"
"I shall uphold this so that others may hear the *Dharmaparyāya on the Meritorious Names of Akṣobhya Buddha*.
People of meager merit will never be able to hear this sutra, nor will they be able to receive, uphold, or recite it."
When Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas hear this *Dharmaparyāya on the Virtuous Name of Akṣobhya Buddha*, they shall accomplish the practice of *avaivartika* (non-retrogression);
having heard it, by receiving, upholding, and reciting it, they will exclusively attain the practice of the unsurpassed, right, and true path.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“Those who are in their second or third birth before reaching the stage of being destined for enlightenment (ekajātipratibaddha/trijātipratibaddha) cannot be surpassed by those seeking the path of discipleship (śrāvaka) who aspire to perfect awakening.”

If there are those who hear this *Dharmaparyāya on the Meritorious Names of Akṣobhya Buddha*, and having received and upheld it, recite it, and explain it to several hundreds, several thousands, or several hundreds of thousands of people—just so, Śāriputra!
"A Wheel-Turning King naturally gives rise to the seven treasures through his merit.
In the same way, Śāriputra,
it is due to the power of the former vows of the Buddha Akṣobhya that I have preached this Dharma-sūtra of his meritorious titles."

If there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who preach this Dharma-sūtra of the virtuous names, or if there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who hear this sūtra—even those who have only just begun to hear it—it is likewise due to the power of their merit.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:

“In this Bhadrakalpa, all the Buddhas, the Gods among Gods, shall likewise preach this *Dharmaparyāya of the Virtuous Epithets of Akṣobhya Buddha*, ensuring it remains complete and unimpaired, just as I have spoken it.”

If there are bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who wish to quickly attain unexcelled, perfect, true enlightenment and supreme awakening, they should receive this *Dharmaparyāya of the Meritorious Names of Akṣobhya Buddha*, and they should uphold, recite, explain, and cause it to be widely disseminated.

"If this Dharma-sūtra of the Virtuous Name exists within a commandery, a kingdom, a district, or a town, and if there are good sons or good daughters who receive, uphold, recite, and chant it, then those Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas, possessing this sūtra, shall protect that commandery, kingdom, district, or town."

“Whoever receives this Dharma-sūtra of the Virtuous Name and shall uphold, recite, and further leave the household life to study the Way and depart from evil—such Bodhisattvas Mahāsattvas should cause those who study the Way while remaining at home to know this.”
"Why is this? Because, Śāriputra, sons and daughters of good family will not be able to fully comprehend this Dharma-sūtra of the Virtuous Title.
The Buddha said to Śāriputra:
“If there are those in distant provinces, kingdoms, districts, or towns who practice this sutra, a bodhisattva mahāsattva should go to them, receive this sutra, recite it, uphold it, and explain it.”
Good sons and good daughters, even if they do not recite it, they should provide offerings whenever this scripture is present;

if they cannot obtain a copy of the scripture, they should then transcribe it. If someone does not give them a copy of the scripture to take back and transcribe, the Bodhisattva shall go to that person’s home and transcribe it there.
If a good son or good daughter says they will transcribe it by fasting, they shall transcribe it while fasting.
If it says "to copy while walking," one should copy while walking;
if it says "to copy while standing," one should copy while standing;
if it says "to copy while sitting," one should copy while sitting.
The Sūtra on the Land of Akṣobhya Buddha, Scroll II.
